title: Academic WorldQuest 2026-27 — Region in Focus: The European Union
format: Multiple choice, four options; 'answer' gives the correct option letter
sources: S1: European Parliament video on EU trade policy (transcript)
S3: Council of the EU — EU relations with the United States (last review 11 Oct 2026)
S4: European Union — History of the EU
S5: Lithuanian Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Membership
S6: European Union — How EU policy is decided
S7: European Council — Press statement by President Costa after meeting President Nausėda (26 Aug 2026)
S8: European Union — Types of institutions and bodies

questions.question: According to the European Parliament, approximately what share of world trade did the EU represent in 2024?
questions.explanation: The EU represented an estimated 15.8% of world trade in 2024, making it the world's largest trading bloc.

questions.question: How many jobs in the EU were supported by exports to non-EU countries in 2023?
questions.explanation: Exports outside the EU supported 33.5 million jobs, or 15.4% of all EU employment.

questions.question: Roughly what fraction of jobs in the EU depend on trade with countries outside the Union?
questions.explanation: With 15.4% of EU employment supported by exports, almost one in six EU jobs depends on trade.

questions.question: More than how many European businesses export outside the EU?
questions.explanation: Over 630,000 European businesses export to markets outside the EU.

questions.question: The EU currently has over 40 trade agreements covering more than how many countries?
questions.explanation: The EU has over 40 trade agreements with more than 70 countries on six continents.

questions.question: Why does the EU negotiate trade as a single bloc rather than through 27 national trade strategies?

options.A: EU treaties forbid member states from trading
options.B: The single market gives the EU a stronger negotiating position than any one country alone
options.C: The WTO only recognizes regional blocs

questions.explanation: Acting in a united way, backed by the single market, puts the EU in a better negotiating position.

questions.question: In the EU trade-agreement process, which institution asks the Council for permission to open negotiations and then negotiates on behalf of the whole EU?

options.D: Court of Justice of the EU

questions.explanation: The Commission requests a green light from the Council and then negotiates for the EU.

questions.question: Which EU institution must give its consent before any trade deal can enter into force, and can reject deals whose concerns are not addressed?
questions.explanation: The European Parliament is responsible for ratifying all trade deals and for trade-related legislation.

questions.question: Some trade agreements must be approved by all EU member states individually. Which of these areas triggers that requirement?
questions.explanation: Agreements covering trade in services, commercial aspects of intellectual property, and foreign direct investment require approval by all member states.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the EU's anti-coercion instrument?

options.A: To fine EU companies that violate competition law
options.B: To let the EU respond with countermeasures when a country uses trade threats to pressure it
options.C: To screen migrants at external borders

questions.explanation: If a partner tries to blackmail the EU through trade, the EU can respond with tariffs, quotas, and limits on access to services, public programs, financial markets, or IP rights.

questions.question: In May 2026 the European Parliament adopted new foreign investment screening rules primarily to prevent what?

options.B: Hostile foreign actors buying Europe's critical infrastructure

questions.explanation: The rules aim to stop hostile foreign governments or companies from acquiring ports, airports, communication networks, and other critical infrastructure.

questions.question: The EU recently concluded trade talks with which country, described as the world's largest democracy and fourth-largest economy, creating a market of about 2 billion people?
questions.explanation: The EU–India agreement creates a combined market of roughly 2 billion people.

questions.question: In June 2026, the EU signed a new digital trade agreement with which country?
questions.explanation: The EU signed a digital trade agreement with South Korea in June 2026.

questions.question: Mercosur, with which the EU has a trade deal, is a trading bloc located in which region?
questions.explanation: Mercosur is the South American trading bloc.

questions.question: Which industry was the subject of recent European Parliament legislation, justified by its investment in the green transition and its role supplying the European defence industry?
questions.explanation: Parliament adopted new laws addressing steel markets to protect competitiveness and secure supply.

questions.question: Besides tariffs, which of the following do EU trade agreements typically do?

options.A: Set member states' income tax rates
options.B: Let European companies bid for government contracts in partner countries
options.C: Grant partner citizens EU voting rights
options.D: Replace national currencies with the euro

questions.explanation: Trade agreements also cover public procurement access, product safety standards, and protection for workers and farmers.

questions.question: Together, the EU and the US account for roughly what share of global GDP?
questions.explanation: The EU and US represent 43% of global GDP and almost 30% of global trade in goods and services.

questions.question: According to provisional Council data, what was the value of EU–US trade in goods and services in 2025?
questions.explanation: Bilateral trade reached a record €1.77 trillion in 2025 — more than the GDP of Spain.

questions.question: The value of EU–US trade in 2025 exceeded the entire GDP of which EU member state?
questions.explanation: The Council notes that 2025 transatlantic trade was larger than Spain's GDP.

questions.question: Taking both goods and services into account, what was the EU's trade balance with the US in 2025?
questions.explanation: The EU had a €20 billion surplus with the US across goods and services combined.

questions.question: On what date was the EU–US joint statement on a framework for 'reciprocal, fair and balanced' trade issued?
questions.explanation: The joint statement dates from 21 August 2025; the Council adopted the implementing regulations in June 2026.

questions.question: The 2026 regulations implementing the EU–US joint statement extended the suspension of EU duties on which seafood product, from all countries?
questions.explanation: The duty suspension on lobster imports was extended, applying retroactively from 1 August 2025 and expiring in July 2030 unless renewed.

questions.question: Under its sunset clause, until when will the main regulation enacting EU tariff reductions on US industrial goods apply unless further action is taken?
questions.explanation: The main regulation applies until the end of 2029; it also includes safeguard and suspension mechanisms.

questions.question: Mutual EU–US foreign direct investment stocks in 2024 exceeded €4.8 trillion — almost equal to the combined economies of which two countries?
questions.explanation: EU–US FDI stocks are almost equal to the entire economies of France and Spain combined.

questions.question: Total US investment in the EU is almost how many times larger than US investment in the Asia-Pacific region?
questions.explanation: US investment in the EU is almost four times higher than in Asia-Pacific; EU investment in the US is about ten times its investment in India and China combined.

questions.question: How many people are employed by EU companies' investments in the United States?
questions.explanation: EU investments employ 3.4 million people in the US, while US exports to the EU support 2.3 million US jobs.

questions.question: In 2025, US liquefied natural gas made up almost what share of the EU's LNG imports?
questions.explanation: The EU imported 82.9 bcm of US LNG — 26.4% of total gas imports and almost 58% of LNG imports.

questions.question: What forum do the EU and US use to coordinate on strategic energy issues and research cooperation?
questions.explanation: The EU–US Energy Council coordinates strategic energy issues and R&D cooperation.

questions.question: The EU and US have invested $600 billion worldwide through which G7 initiative, including via the EU's Global Gateway?

options.B: Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment

questions.explanation: The investment runs through the G7 Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment.

questions.question: Since the start of Russia's war of aggression, the EU and its member states have provided over how much in support for Ukraine?
questions.explanation: EU and member state support for Ukraine exceeds €215 billion.

questions.question: Which of the following is an EU–US academic exchange programme highlighted by the Council?
questions.explanation: The Fulbright-Schuman programme is listed alongside Erasmus+, Jean Monnet actions, and Marie Skłodowska-Curie actions.

questions.question: In the European Parliament's trade video, a Member called the US 'Liberation Day' tariff announcement of 2 April 2025 by what alternative name, citing rising US prices?
questions.explanation: The MEP referred to it as 'inflation day' and noted the US Supreme Court had removed its legal basis.

questions.question: The membership criteria that any European country must meet to join the EU are commonly known as what?
questions.explanation: The Copenhagen criteria require stable democratic institutions, a functioning market economy, and the ability to take on membership obligations.

questions.question: To which body must a country wishing to join the EU submit its membership application?

options.D: Court of Justice of the EU

questions.explanation: Applications go to the Council, which asks the Commission to assess the applicant.

questions.question: What level of agreement among EU member states is required to grant a country candidate status?
questions.explanation: All EU member states must agree on the decision to grant candidate status and begin negotiations.

questions.question: The body of EU laws and standards that a candidate country must adopt during negotiations is called what?
questions.explanation: During membership negotiations, candidates prepare to implement the acquis.

questions.question: What document details the terms and conditions of a new country's EU membership and sets its joining date?
questions.explanation: The accession treaty must be approved by EU institutions and ratified by all member states and the candidate.

questions.question: How many enlargements have taken place since the EU's six founding members?
questions.explanation: Seven enlargements have brought the EU to 27 member countries.

questions.question: Which country joined the EU in the most recent enlargement, on 1 July 2013?
questions.explanation: Croatia's accession was the seventh enlargement.

questions.question: Which two countries joined the EU together on 1 January 2007 in the sixth enlargement?
questions.explanation: Bulgaria and Romania joined in 2007.

questions.question: The 2004 enlargement, the largest in terms of people and number of countries, added how many new members?
questions.explanation: Ten countries joined on 1 May 2004, including Poland, the Czech Republic, and the three Baltic states.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT among the ten countries that joined the EU on 1 May 2004?
questions.explanation: Croatia joined in 2013; Malta, Cyprus, and Slovakia joined in 2004.

questions.question: Western Balkan partners follow a unique enlargement track known as what?
questions.explanation: The stabilisation and association process (SAP) supports political and economic stability in the region.

questions.question: Which Western Balkan partner is currently the EU's only 'potential candidate' — having applied but not yet received candidate status?
questions.explanation: Kosovo is listed as a potential candidate; the other three are candidate countries.

questions.question: Which of these countries has been granted EU candidate status?
questions.explanation: The nine candidates are Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Türkiye, and Ukraine.

questions.question: How many aspiring members are currently involved in the EU accession process?
questions.explanation: Ten aspiring members are in the process: nine candidates plus one potential candidate.

questions.question: What European Commission plan aims to prepare Western Balkan partners for accession through economic reforms and investment?

options.B: Growth Plan for the Western Balkans

questions.explanation: The Growth Plan seeks to bring some benefits of membership to the region before accession.

questions.question: On 25 March 1957, six countries signed the Treaty of Rome, establishing which organization?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Rome established the European Economic Community (EEC), forerunner of today's EU.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT one of the EU's six founding members?
questions.explanation: The founders were Belgium, France, Germany, Italy, Luxembourg, and the Netherlands.

questions.question: Post-war cooperation in the period 1945–59 first produced which European organization, before the Treaties of Rome?
questions.explanation: The European Coal and Steel Community preceded the Treaties of Rome and the European Parliament.

questions.question: Which three countries became the first new members of the Community in the 1970s?
questions.explanation: Denmark, Ireland, and the UK joined in the 1970s.

questions.question: The EU's history page associates the 1990s with which developments?

options.A: The Erasmus programme and collapse of communism
options.B: The single market, border-free travel, and the euro
options.C: The Lisbon Treaty and the financial crisis
options.D: The COVID-19 response and climate action

questions.explanation: The 1990s, 'A Europe without frontiers,' saw the single market, border-free travel, and the euro launched.

questions.question: Between 2000 and 2009, how many new countries joined the EU?
questions.explanation: Twelve countries joined in 2000–09, a decade that also saw the Lisbon Treaty signed.

questions.question: Which EU treaty, signed in 2007, introduced amendments to the powers of the EU's institutions?
questions.explanation: The Lisbon Treaty (2007) amended the founding treaties: the TFEU (1957) and TEU (1992).

questions.question: In what year was the EU awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for advancing peace, reconciliation, democracy, and human rights in Europe?
questions.explanation: The EU received the 2012 Nobel Peace Prize.

questions.question: On what date did Lithuania become a full member of the EU?
questions.explanation: Lithuania joined in the 2004 enlargement.

questions.question: Lithuania will take over the presidency of the Council of the EU in which month?
questions.explanation: President Costa noted Lithuania is preparing to take over the Council presidency in January 2027; its previous presidency was in 2013.

questions.question: Before joining the EU, Lithuania's GDP per capita was 42% of the EU average. What had it risen to by 2013?
questions.explanation: It rose to 62% in 2011 and 73% in 2013.

questions.question: In what year did Lithuania join the Schengen zone, allowing its citizens to travel freely across Europe?
questions.explanation: Lithuania joined Schengen in 2007.

questions.question: The NordBalt energy interconnection links Lithuania with which country?
questions.explanation: NordBalt links Sweden and Lithuania; LitPol links Poland and Lithuania.

questions.question: What 2009 plan approved by the European Commission aimed to integrate the Baltic States' energy market with the rest of the EU?
questions.explanation: BEMIP supported projects such as NordBalt, LitPol, regional LNG terminals, and a Poland–Lithuania gas interconnector.

questions.question: About what share of foreign direct investment into Lithuania has come from other EU member states?
questions.explanation: About 80% of FDI in Lithuania originated in EU member states.

questions.question: Thanks to EU citizenship, a Lithuanian national in a country where Lithuania has no embassy can get consular help from other EU missions. Which country does Lithuania's Foreign Ministry cite as an example?
questions.explanation: The ministry lists Chile, Saudi Arabia, and Nepal as examples.

questions.question: President Costa said Lithuania's geography exposes it to the 'instrumentalisation' of what, calling it a common European challenge?
questions.explanation: Costa said instrumentalised migration is unacceptable on any EU external border, citing Ceuta and the Baltic region.

questions.question: President Costa called agreement on the EU's next long-term budget the decisive challenge of autumn 2026. What period does that budget cover?
questions.explanation: Agreement on the 2028–2034 budget is needed by the end of 2026 to avoid interrupting funding in 2028.

questions.question: What term describes the new revenue streams that Costa said would be essential to financing the EU's next budget?
questions.explanation: A package of 'new own resources' is to be part of the overall budget agreement.

questions.question: Which three institutions reach agreement on legislation under the EU's ordinary legislative procedure?

options.A: European Council, ECB, Court of Justice
options.B: European Parliament, Council of the EU, European Commission
options.C: European Commission, Court of Auditors, European Council

questions.explanation: Parliament represents citizens, the Council represents governments, and the Commission represents the EU's overall interest.

questions.question: Before proposing new initiatives, the European Commission prepares a report setting out the advantages and disadvantages of policy options. What is it called?
questions.explanation: Impact assessments incorporate input from NGOs, national authorities, industry, and expert groups.

questions.question: If the Parliament and Council cannot agree on amendments during the second reading, what is set up to try to find a solution?
questions.explanation: A conciliation committee attempts to reconcile the two positions; either institution may block the proposal at this stage.

questions.question: Under the 'consent' special legislative procedure, what may the European Parliament do?

options.B: Only accept or reject the proposal as it stands

questions.explanation: Under consent, Parliament cannot amend; under consultation, it gives an opinion the Council need not follow.

questions.question: Where must an EU law be published once Parliament and Council agree on a joint text?

options.B: The Official Journal of the EU

questions.explanation: A proposal becomes law once agreed and published in the Official Journal.

questions.question: Which EU institution generally does NOT make laws but determines the EU's overall political direction?
questions.explanation: The European Council sets political direction and can agree on treaty changes but does not legislate.

questions.question: In which city is the European Central Bank located?
questions.explanation: The ECB is in Frankfurt; the Court of Justice and Court of Auditors are in Luxembourg.

questions.question: Approximately how many EU civil servants and other staff serve the EU's roughly 450 million people?
questions.explanation: About 60,000 staff serve the EU — fewer than the French Finance Ministry's roughly 140,000.

questions.question: The European Medicines Agency, a decentralised EU agency established in 1995, is based in which city?
questions.explanation: The EMA in Amsterdam ensures the safety and efficacy of human and veterinary medicines.
